facts.fact_text: The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) is a political party in the Republic of Moldova.
On 3 December 2003, the applicant party applied to the Chișinău Municipal Council for an authorisation to hold a protest demonstration.
The applicant party requested to hold the protest demonstration in the Square of the Great National Assembly, in front of the Government's building.
The applicant party requested to hold the protest demonstration on 25 January 2004.
According to the application, the organisers intended to express views on the functioning of the democratic institutions in Moldova.
According to the application, the organisers intended to express views on the respect for human rights.
According to the application, the organisers intended to express views on the Moldo-Russian conflict in Transdniestria.
On 20 January 2004, the Chișinău Municipal Council rejected the applicant party's request to hold a protest demonstration.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, they have obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of Sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge in the administrative courts the refusal of the local government.

The Chișinău Municipal Council rejected the applicant party's request on the ground that it had convincing evidence that during the meeting there would be calls to a war of aggression, ethnic hatred and public violence.

Section 7(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances involving incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds.
Section 7(c) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances involving incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence.
Section 7(d) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances involving acts that undermine the constitutional order.

The Chișinău Municipal Council rejected the applicant party's request on the ground that it had convincing evidence that during the meeting there would be calls to a war of aggression, ethnic hatred and public violence.
The applicant party argued, inter alia, that the reasons relied upon by the Chișinău Municipal Council for refusing the authorisation were entirely baseless.
According to the Chișinău Court of Appeal, the slogan 'Down with Voronin's totalitarian regime' constituted a call to a violent overthrow of the constitutional regime.
According to the Chișinău Court of Appeal, the slogan 'Down with Putin's occupation regime' constituted a call to hatred towards the Russian people.

The applicant party argued, inter alia, that the slogans 'Down with Voronin's totalitarian regime' and 'Down with Putin's occupation regime' could not have reasonably been interpreted as a call to a violent overthrow of the Government.

The applicant party argued, inter alia, that the slogans 'Down with Voronin's totalitarian regime' and 'Down with Putin's occupation regime' could not have reasonably been interpreted as a call to ethnic hatred.
